correctness.rationale: After common-modulus normalization, Fourier zeros are roots of a cubic on the \(N\)-th roots of unity. For three unit-circle roots, Vieta gives \(|e_2|=|e_1|\) and \(|e_3|=1\), so equal coefficient moduli reduce to \(|e_1|=1\). The exact trigonometric factorization \(1+\cos\alpha+\cos\beta+\cos(\alpha-\beta)=2\cos((\alpha-\beta)/2)(\cos((\alpha+\beta)/2)+\cos((\alpha-\beta)/2))\) forces an antipodal root pair. Conversely an antipodal pair makes all Vieta coefficients unimodular. The parity classification then follows because the \(N\)-th roots contain an antipodal pair iff \(N\) is even, with explicit witnesses for every smaller count.

value.rationale: Equal-magnitude coefficients form the standard phase-only subclass in Fourier extremal problems. Four consecutive frequencies are the first case in which a cubic can create three sampled zeros. The theorem gives a complete all-modulus classification and identifies parity, through antipodal root geometry, as the sole obstruction to the maximal zero count. This is a structural classification rather than a small-modulus table or a numerical increment.
